title: Вестибулярный синдром
terminology: Вестибулярный синдром описывает совокупность признаков и локализацию, но не этиологию.
Первое решение — peripheral, central или uncertain localization по полному неврологическому осмотру, а не по возрасту, стороне наклона головы или направлению нистагма отдельно.
Idiopathic peripheral vestibular syndrome допускается только при остром непроявляющем боли периферическом паттерне без центральных признаков и с ожидаемым улучшением; это диагноз исключения.
Серийное течение является частью доказательства: отсутствие улучшения, рецидив или новые deficits переоткрывают локализацию.
Остаточный наклон головы после общего улучшения не равен неудаче лечения и не создаёт случайный центральный диагноз.
Нормальный наружный канал и барабанная перепонка не исключают заболевание среднего/внутреннего уха.
Facial nerve deficit и Horner syndrome поддерживают периферический ear route, тогда как altered mentation, postural deficits и дополнительные cranial nerves повышают центральную вероятность.
Otitis interna обычно не меняет сознание; лихорадка, вялость и дополнительные deficits требуют оценки внутричерепного распространения.
MRI/CT и CSF являются отдельными внешними маршрутами; безопасность CSF оценивается после imaging review.
Гидратация, тошнота, аспирация, способность стоять, есть и пить, падения и травмы определяют немедленную безопасность независимо от причины.
Токсическая экспозиция, травма, врождённый паттерн и системная болезнь требуют собственных доказательств и не генерируются задним числом.
Система не генерирует antiemetic, antimicrobial, steroid, ear procedure, CSF protocol, препарат, дозу или технику.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Каковы точное начало, progression и owner video?
Может ли пациент стоять, ходить, есть и пить; есть ли рвота, аспирация или падения?
Изменились ли mentation, поведение или появились судороги?
Каковы направление, положение и изменчивость нистагма?
Есть ли postural deficits или дополнительные cranial nerve signs?
Есть ли ear pain, discharge, chronic recurrence и изменение слуха?
Есть ли facial weakness, Horner signs и риск для роговицы?
Какие ear cleaners, лекарства или токсины использовались и когда?
Была ли травма головы или риск повреждения temporal bone?
Есть ли fever, weight/appetite change, systemic или thyroid context?
Каковы прежние imaging, CSF, ear samples или polyp history?
Безопасен ли дом и возможны ли recheck, transport и referral?

variants.title: Острый улучшающийся idiopathic peripheral syndrome
variants.diagnosticTruth: Idiopathic peripheral vestibular syndrome requires acute onset, peripheral localization, absence of central evidence and serial improvement; age and head tilt only modify context.

presentations.complaint: An older dog acutely falls, tilts the head and has peripheral signs without pain or central deficits.

followUp.timing: daily observable course with prompt reassessment if not improving

outcomes.safe: Idiopathic label follows localization and improvement.
outcomes.unsafe: Old age alone closes the case.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the pattern may improve, but improvement and absence of new neurologic signs are part of the diagnosis.

presentations.complaint: A cat of any age has an acute peripheral pattern and begins to improve without central signs.

examFindings.finding: Age does not confirm idiopathic cause.

followUp.timing: short serial course with feeding and central red-flag checks

outcomes.safe: Cat improves after ear and central routes remain negative.
outcomes.unsafe: Every acute feline tilt is idiopathic.

ownerCommunication: Explain that cats can have polyps or ear disease at any age, so improvement and ear assessment both matter.

presentations.complaint: General recovery occurs but head tilt persists, or signs recur/incompletely resolve.

outcomes.safe: Residual tilt is accepted while relapse reopens workup.
outcomes.unsafe: Residual tilt becomes random failure or recurrence is ignored.

ownerCommunication: Explain that a tilt may remain despite recovery, but recurrence or new signs require reassessment.

variants.title: Среднее/внутреннее ухо и периферическая локализация
variants.diagnosticTruth: Peripheral vestibular signs with facial/Horner findings or chronic ear context require middle/inner-ear imaging and site-specific sampling; normal external appearance and external samples do not exclude or define middle-ear disease.

presentations.complaint: Peripheral vestibular signs coexist with facial nerve deficit, Horner syndrome or hearing change.

historyAnswers.mentation_behavior_and_seizure_change: Mentation remains normal or central red flag shown.

examFindings.finding: Peripheral localization is not final cause.

outcomes.safe: Cranial signs guide a confirmed ear route.
outcomes.unsafe: External ear appearance alone names the cause.

ownerCommunication: Explain that these nerves pass near the middle/inner ear and imaging may be needed even when the canal looks acceptable.

presentations.complaint: Chronic recurrent ear disease precedes vestibular signs despite an apparently normal or inaccessible canal.

outcomes.unsafe: A normal canal or external swab closes the case.

ownerCommunication: Explain that disease can remain behind an intact-looking eardrum and requires a different sample site.

presentations.complaint: Ear-associated vestibular disease has severe pain, fever, lethargy or new central/multiple cranial nerve signs.

outcomes.safe: Intracranial extension is treated as emergency uncertainty.
outcomes.unsafe: Fever and central signs are ignored because ear disease exists.

ownerCommunication: Explain that infection/inflammation may have extended beyond the ear and urgent imaging and hospital care are needed.

variants.title: Центральный вестибулярный синдром
variants.diagnosticTruth: Altered mentation, postural deficits, additional cranial nerves, paradoxical cerebellar or multifocal findings require central localization and urgent advanced referral; vascular, inflammatory, infectious, neoplastic and metabolic causes remain separate.

presentations.complaint: Vestibular signs coexist with altered mentation, postural deficits or additional cranial nerve abnormalities.

outcomes.unsafe: Old age or horizontal nystagmus forces idiopathic label.

ownerCommunication: Explain that additional neurologic abnormalities point inside the brain rather than only the balance organ.

presentations.complaint: Vestibular signs conflict with simple side rules or include cerebellar/multifocal abnormalities.

examFindings.finding: Head tilt side is not lesion proof.

outcomes.safe: Complex signs prevent simplistic side assignment.
outcomes.unsafe: Tilt direction becomes a definitive lesion map.

ownerCommunication: Explain that mixed signs make bedside side rules unreliable and require advanced localization.

presentations.complaint: Central localization requires distinction among vascular, inflammatory, infectious, neoplastic and metabolic routes.

outcomes.unsafe: Central syndrome randomly chooses tumor, stroke or infection.

ownerCommunication: Explain that localization tells where the problem is, while imaging and selected tests determine why.

variants.title: Токсическая, травматическая, врождённая или системная причина
variants.diagnosticTruth: Ototoxic exposure, trauma, congenital bilateral disease and selected systemic conditions require an observed timeline and compatible localization; they are not inferred after results and do not bypass central safety assessment.

presentations.complaint: Vestibular signs follow a documented ear cleaner or potentially ototoxic medication exposure.

outcomes.safe: Documented exposure is evaluated without generated antidote.
outcomes.unsafe: System invents a cleaner or medication after the event.

ownerCommunication: Ask for the exact product and timing and explain that exposure must match the clinical course.

presentations.complaint: Vestibular signs follow head trauma or suspected temporal bone injury.

examFindings.finding: Peripheral appearance does not exclude injury.

followUp.timing: emergency imaging and serial neurologic status

outcomes.safe: Trauma receives brain and skull safety assessment.
outcomes.unsafe: Head tilt is observed at home after trauma.

ownerCommunication: Explain that balance signs after head injury can reflect skull or brain damage and require urgent imaging.

presentations.complaint: Bilateral, congenital or systemic-context vestibular signs require a broader non-idiopathic route.

outcomes.unsafe: Hypothyroidism or congenital disease is assigned from vestibular signs alone.

ownerCommunication: Explain why bilateral or lifelong signs require a different, context-driven workup.

variants.title: Кошачий полип/масса или атипичное течение
variants.diagnosticTruth: Feline respiratory/ear history, polyp or skull-base mass and failure to improve require ear/skull-base imaging and site-specific referral; an idiopathic label cannot survive progression, relapse or new central signs.

presentations.complaint: A cat has vestibular signs with respiratory/ear history compatible with a nasopharyngeal or middle-ear polyp.

outcomes.safe: Polyp is confirmed by site-specific route.
outcomes.unsafe: Young cat plus ear history generates a polyp procedure.

ownerCommunication: Explain that a polyp is plausible but needs visualization or imaging before a procedural decision.

presentations.complaint: Progressive vestibular, facial or multiple cranial deficits raise an ear/skull-base mass route.

outcomes.safe: Progressive mass route is imaged and sampled safely.
outcomes.unsafe: Imaging appearance becomes final tumor type.

ownerCommunication: Explain that progression and several affected nerves require skull-base imaging and, if safe, tissue identification.

presentations.complaint: A presumed peripheral feline course fails to improve, relapses or develops new central signs.

outcomes.unsafe: Idiopathic label persists because it was assigned first.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the observed course no longer fits the earlier working diagnosis and requires a new localization.

familyValidationRules: Reject if age, head tilt or nystagmus direction alone proves idiopathic disease or lesion side.
Reject if central signs are ignored or idiopathic label persists without improvement or after new deficits.
Reject if a normal external canal excludes middle-ear disease.
Reject if residual head tilt alone becomes treatment failure or a new random central diagnosis.
Reject if all cats or dogs recover on an identical fixed timeline.
Reject if MRI, CT or CSF is instant or CSF lacks imaging safety review.
Reject if code generates antiemetic, antimicrobial, steroid, ear procedure, CSF protocol, drug or dose.
